title: Heavier Rope? Tension Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
At her grandmother's village Diya pulls a bucket of water up from the well. Holding it still is easy, but when she starts to pull it up faster, the rope feels heavier, though the water has not changed. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn tension: the pull of a string or rope, along the rope and away from the body, the same all along a light rope.

On a live motion notebook a 5 kg bucket rises on a rope over a smooth pulley. A slow-mo replay draws T, mg, a and v while the readout and the T vs a graph move together: T is 49 N hanging still or at a steady speed, 59 N speeding up, 39 N slowing down. We derive T = m(g + a) step by step, compare pulling up faster with lowering faster, answer two pause-and-think questions, work out how hard Diya must pull, see the exam trap about moving up, solve an original JEE Main pattern question on a rope that can break and finish with a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 The rope feels heavier. Why?
0:29 What is tension?
0:54 Motion notebook: the bucket on the rope
1:11 Slow-mo: T = 59 N, a = 2 m/s²
1:40 Pause and think: steady speed
1:59 The rule, step by step
2:45 Side by side + pause and think
3:21 Worked example: over a smooth pulley
3:57 Exam trap: moving up means T > mg?
4:19 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:02 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Static and Kinetic Friction. A heavy steel trunk is hard to start, but easier to keep sliding. Why?
